title: Physical Custody
statement: Who the child lives with.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet, Juvenile Dependency Court and You, p. 29
source_says: Who the child will live with (called physical custody)
steps: Searched for the booklet, opened the courts.ca.gov PDF, read the exit order passage on p. 29.

title: Physical Custody
statement: An exit order says which parent has it.
source_says: the judge will make an exit order
steps: Same PDF, p. 29. Exit order text lists who the child will live with (physical custody) among the things it decides.

title: Physical Custody
statement: Who the child lives with.
source_says: Who the child will live with (called physical custody)
steps: Same PDF, p. 29.

title: Police Officer
statement: Police can receive reports about a child's safety and look into them.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; Penal Code 11165.9
source_says: usually made to the police or to social workers ... They are required to investigate these reports.
steps: Searched selfhelp.courts.ca.gov parents guide, opened it, read the reports paragraph. Also opened Penal Code 11165.9 on california.public.law: police and sheriff departments shall accept reports.

title: Police Officer
statement: A police officer can take a child into protective custody when the child is in immediate danger.
source_says: Any peace officer may, without a warrant, take into temporary custody a minor ... the minor is in immediate danger of physical or sexual abuse
steps: Searched WIC 305, opened the public.law page, read the opening line and subdivision (a).

title: Police Officer
statement: After that, the county social worker and the court handle the case.
source_says: The social worker must file the petition within two court days of removing your child.
steps: Opened WIC 306 on public.law (social worker may receive a child delivered by a peace officer) and the parents guide (social worker files the petition).

title: Police Officer
statement: Police can step in when a child is in danger right now. Then the social worker takes over.
source_says: the minor has an immediate need for medical care, or the minor is in immediate danger of physical or sexual abuse
steps: Same WIC 305 page, subdivision (a).

title: Post-Adoption Contact Agreement
statement: A written agreement between birth parents and adoptive parents about contact after an adoption, such as visits, calls, or letters.
source_says: a written agreement to permit continuing contact ... Provisions for visitation between the child and a birth parent or parents
steps: Searched Family Code 8616.5, opened public.law page. Statute also lets other birth relatives, siblings, the tribe and the child be parties; entry names only birth parents, which is narrower but not contradicted.

title: Post-Adoption Contact Agreement
statement: It only exists if the adoptive parents agree to it.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet, p. 16; Family Code 8616.5(b)(1)
source_says: but only if the people adopting your child agree to what's called a post-adoption contact agreement.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 16. Family Code 8616.5 also requires the agreement be executed voluntarily.

title: Post-Adoption Contact Agreement
statement: A written deal about staying in touch after an adoption.
source_says: a written agreement to permit continuing contact
steps: Same public.law page.

title: Post-Permanency Review Hearing
statement: A review hearing held every six months after a permanent plan is in place, for as long as the court keeps the case open.
source_says: the status of the child shall be reviewed at least every six months
steps: Searched WIC 366.3, opened public.law page, read (a) and (d)(1). Booklet p. 18 says a hearing every six months after a permanent plan is made.

title: Post-Permanency Review Hearing
statement: The judge checks that the child is getting what they need and that the plan is still right.
source_says: The continuing appropriateness and extent of compliance with the permanent plan for the child
steps: Same page, subdivision (e) list of what the court must determine.

title: Post-Permanency Review Hearing
statement: If a parent's rights were ended, that parent no longer gets notice of these hearings.
source_says: Unless their parental rights have been permanently terminated, the parent or parents of the child are entitled to receive notice of, and participate in, those hearings
steps: Same page, subdivision (f). Booklet p. 18: 'you won't be told when court hearings happen'.

title: Post-Permanency Review Hearing
statement: A check-in hearing every six months after the permanent plan is chosen.
source_says: the court will have a hearing every six months after a permanent plan is made for your child
steps: Opened booklet PDF, p. 18.

title: Preponderance of the Evidence
statement: A level of proof that means more likely than not.
source_name: Judicial Council, Primer on Juvenile Dependency Proceedings for Caregivers, p. 9
source_says: proving that it is more probable than not
steps: Searched courts.ca.gov for a definition, opened the Judicial Council caregiver primer, read the preponderance definition on p. 9. WIC 355 itself does not define the term.

title: Preponderance of the Evidence
statement: At the jurisdiction hearing the county has to show by this level that what the petition says is true.
source_name: WIC 355(a); Judicial Council Beyond the Bench hearing outline
source_says: The Agency bears the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the allegations in the petition are true.
steps: Opened WIC 355 on public.law: 'Proof by a preponderance of evidence must be adduced' but it does not name who carries the burden. Opened the courts.ca.gov training outline for the burden.

title: Preponderance of the Evidence
statement: You do not have to prove you are innocent.
source_name: Judicial Council Beyond the Bench hearing outline; WIC 355(a)
source_says: The Agency bears the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the allegations in the petition are true.
steps: Same sources. The burden is on the agency. Note WIC 355.1 has some presumptions that shift the burden of producing evidence; not opened in this run.

title: Preponderance of the Evidence
statement: More likely true than not. The county has to show this.
source_name: Judicial Council Beyond the Bench hearing outline
source_says: The Agency bears the burden to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the allegations in the petition are true.
steps: Same sources as the definition.

title: Presumed Parent
statement: A person the law treats as a child's legal parent.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet, p. 31; Family Code 7611
source_says: also called a presumed parent
steps: Opened booklet p. 31 and Family Code 7611 on public.law (person 'presumed to be the natural parent').

title: Presumed Parent
statement: Common ways to be a presumed parent: your name is on the birth certificate, you were married to the birth parent when the child was conceived or born, a family court named you a parent, or you raised the child as your own.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: Your name is on your child's birth certificate ... There is a family court order that establishes a parental relationship ... You have acted like the child is your own
steps: Searched selfhelp.courts.ca.gov, opened the guide for fathers and other parents; its four 'most common ways' match the entry. Note: Family Code 7611(c)(1) on public.law counts the birth certificate only together with marriage after birth, so the cited statute alone does not support the birth certificate item.

title: Presumed Parent
statement: A presumed parent can get reunification services and visits and can ask for custody.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for fathers and other parents
source_says: you have the right to reunification services ... You also have the right to visitation and custody.
steps: Same selfhelp page.

title: Presumed Parent
statement: You do not have to be related by blood.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for fathers and other parents
source_says: you may qualify as a parent even if you are not biologically related to the child
steps: Same selfhelp page.

title: Presumed Parent
statement: Someone the law counts as the child's parent, even without a blood tie.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for fathers and other parents
source_says: you may qualify as a parent even if you are not biologically related to the child
steps: Same selfhelp page.

title: Probation Officer
statement: An officer who supervises young people in the juvenile justice system.
source_name: Form JV-060-INFO, Juvenile Justice Court: Information for Parents
source_says: They also supervise children to see if they are doing what the court has ordered them to do.
steps: Searched courts.ca.gov for the probation officer role, opened JV-060-INFO. Also opened rule 5.530(b)(4): 'The probation officer or social worker' may be present.

title: Probation Officer
statement: A youth who has both a dependency case and a juvenile justice case may have a probation officer and a social worker.
source_says: to be supervised in the juvenile justice system, or to be supervised and served in both systems
steps: Opened JV-060-INFO on courts.ca.gov: the court might decide the child is served in both systems. Also opened WIC 241.1 on public.law: (d) bars being both dependent and ward unless (e) the county has a signed dual-status protocol. Entry says 'may', so it holds, but it is true only in dual-status counties.

title: Probation Officer
statement: The court decides which system takes the lead.
source_says: The recommendations of both departments shall be presented to the juvenile court ... which status is appropriate for the minor
steps: Same page, subdivision (a): probation and child welfare each recommend, the court determines which status is appropriate.

title: Probation Officer
statement: The officer for youth with a juvenile justice case. Some youth have one and a social worker too.
source_says: to be supervised in the juvenile justice system, or to be supervised and served in both systems
steps: Opened JV-060-INFO note on children in both systems. 'Some youth' matches the limited dual status in WIC 241.1(e).

title: Protective Custody
statement: When a child is taken into temporary care by police or a social worker because the child is in immediate danger.
source_says: is in immediate danger of physical or sexual abuse
steps: Opened WIC 305 and WIC 306 on public.law. 305: any peace officer may take temporary custody without a warrant. 306(a): social worker may do so on the same immediate-danger grounds.

title: Protective Custody
statement: This happens before any court hearing and the agency must file a petition within 2 court days.
source_says: The social worker must file the petition within two court days of removing your child.
steps: Opened parents guide. Also opened WIC 313 on leginfo: release within 48 hours, not counting nonjudicial days, unless a petition is filed.

title: Protective Custody
statement: When police or a social worker take a child somewhere safe right away, before any court hearing.
source_says: Any peace officer may, without a warrant, take into temporary custody a minor
steps: Same WIC 305 and 306 pages.

title: Public Health Nurse
statement: A nurse who works with the county child welfare agency to help make sure children in foster care get medical, dental, and mental health care.
source_says: The foster care public health nurse shall work with the appropriate child welfare services workers
steps: Searched WIC 16501.3, opened public.law page. (a) program is to 'promote and enhance the physical, mental, dental, and developmental well-being of children'.

title: Public Health Nurse
statement: The nurse helps keep track of a child's health records and appointments.
source_says: Documenting that each child in foster care receives initial and followup health screenings
steps: Same page, subdivision (c). The word 'appointments' is not in the statute; it lists documenting screenings, collecting health information, and 'Participating in medical care planning and coordinating for the child'.

title: Public Health Nurse
statement: A county nurse who helps make sure kids in foster care get health care.
source_says: coordinate health care services and serve as a liaison with health care professionals
steps: Same page, subdivision (b).

title: Reasonable Efforts
statement: The law requires the county to make reasonable efforts to prevent removal and to help reunify families.
source_says: except as provided in subparagraph (D), reasonable efforts shall be made to preserve and reunify families
steps: Searched 42 USC 671(a)(15), opened law.cornell.edu. (B) requires the efforts but (D) says they 'shall not be required' when a court finds aggravated circumstances and similar. Entry has no source and leaves the exception out.
fix: The law says the county must make reasonable efforts to keep a child safely at home. In most cases it must also try to help the family get back together. In some serious cases the judge can decide the county does not have to offer that help.

title: Reasonable Efforts
statement: The county has to really try to keep families together and help them get back together.
source_says: shall not be required to be made with respect to a parent of a child if a court of competent jurisdiction has determined that
steps: Same page. Subparagraph (D) lists cases where reunification efforts are not required.
fix: The county has to really try to keep families together. In most cases it also has to help them get back together.

title: Referee
statement: A court officer who hears dependency cases in place of a judge.
source_says: A referee shall hear those cases that are assigned to him or her by the presiding judge of the juvenile court
steps: Opened WIC 248 on public.law.

title: Referee
statement: A referee runs the hearing and makes orders.
source_says: with the same powers as a judge of the juvenile court
steps: Same page. Referee must put findings and order in writing.

title: Referee
statement: If a referee hears your case, you may have the right to ask a judge to look at the decision again.
source_says: a written explanation of the right of those persons to seek review of the order by the juvenile court
steps: Opened WIC 248 and WIC 252 on public.law. 252: minor, parent or guardian may apply to the juvenile court for a rehearing.

title: Referee
statement: The deadline is short, so ask your lawyer right away.
source_says: At any time prior to the expiration of 10 days after service of a written copy of the order and findings of a referee
steps: Same WIC 252 page.

title: Referee
statement: Someone who hears cases like a judge does.
source_says: with the same powers as a judge of the juvenile court
steps: Same WIC 248 page.

title: Rehearing
statement: When a referee, not a judge, hears your case, you can ask a judge to hear the matter again.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.542(a); WIC 252
source_says: not acting as a temporary judge
steps: Searched rule 5.542, opened courts.ca.gov rule page. Subdivision (a) covers only a referee 'not acting as a temporary judge'. Entry leaves that out.
fix: When a referee hears your case, you can usually ask a judge to hear it again. You cannot if the referee was acting as a temporary judge, which can happen when the parties agree to it. Ask your lawyer.

title: Rehearing
statement: You have 10 days after you are served with the referee's written order to ask.
source_says: At any time prior to the expiration of 10 days after service of a written copy of the order and findings of a referee
steps: Opened WIC 252 on public.law and rule 5.542 on courts.ca.gov (10 calendar days after service of a copy of the order and findings).

title: Rehearing
statement: Asking a judge to hear it again when a referee decided.
source_says: may apply to the juvenile court for a rehearing
steps: Same WIC 252 page.

title: Relative Caregiver
statement: A family member, like a grandparent, aunt, uncle, or adult sibling, who is caring for a child in a dependency case.
source_says: A "relative" means an adult who is related to the child by blood, adoption, or affinity within the fifth degree of kinship
steps: Searched cdss.ca.gov kinship care, opened the page. Same definition read in WIC 361.3(c)(2) on public.law.

title: Relative Caregiver
statement: Relatives are considered first for placement
source_says: preferential consideration shall be given to a request by a relative of the child for placement ... shall be the first placement to be considered and investigated
steps: Opened WIC 361.3 on public.law, read (a) and (c)(1).

title: Relative Caregiver
statement: and may get financial support similar to foster parents.
source_name: CDSS Caregiver Advocacy Network, Payments page
source_says: directs local child welfare agencies to pay relative caregivers the same rate non-relative caregivers are given
steps: Searched cdss.ca.gov for relative caregiver payments, opened the Payments page. Page ties the same rate to the home meeting approval requirements and the child's eligibility; entry says 'may', which fits.

title: Relative Caregiver
statement: A relative who wants to help should tell the social worker right away and can use form JV-285 to tell the judge.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for relatives; form JV-285
source_says: you must tell the social worker that you want to have the child placed with you ... This will provide the judge with information about you
steps: Searched selfhelp.courts.ca.gov relatives guide, opened it. Also opened the JV-285 form page: 'Relative Information'.

title: Relative Caregiver
statement: A family member, like a grandparent or aunt, who is taking care of the child.
source_says: Kinship care in the foster care system refers to the care of children by relatives
steps: Same CDSS page.

title: Relative Placement
statement: Placing a child with a family member or close family friend when they cannot stay with their parents.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for relatives
source_says: Close family friends and 'non-relative extended family members' may also be entitled to have the child placed in their care.
steps: Opened relatives guide on selfhelp.courts.ca.gov.

title: Relative Placement
statement: California law requires social workers to look for relatives first before placing a child with non-related foster parents.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for relatives; WIC 309(e)(1); WIC 361.3(c)(1)
source_says: must consider placing a child with relatives before considering placing the child with a non-related person
steps: Opened relatives guide. Also opened WIC 309 on public.law: social worker must investigate 'within 30 days' to locate relatives including 'all grandparents'.

title: Relative Placement
statement: This is also called kinship care.
source_says: Kinship care in the foster care system refers to the care of children by relatives
steps: Opened cdss.ca.gov kinship care page. CDSS uses the term for care by relatives; the same page describes nonrelative extended family members separately.

title: Relative Placement
statement: When a child goes to live with family or a close family friend. Social workers have to look for family first.
source_says: get preference when the social worker decides where the child should live
steps: Same relatives guide.

title: Removal
statement: When a social worker or police officer takes a child out of the home because the child is in immediate danger.
source_says: Take your child from you if they think the child is in immediate danger.
steps: Opened parents guide and WIC 305/306 on public.law.

title: Removal
statement: After a removal, the social worker has two court days to file a petition with the court.
source_says: The social worker must file the petition within two court days of removing your child.
steps: Opened parents guide; WIC 313 on leginfo says release within 48 hours excluding nonjudicial days unless a petition is filed.

title: Removal
statement: The child may stay with the other parent, a relative, a close family friend, or a foster home while the case starts.
source_says: The other parent (if they were not part of the reason your child was removed ... A relative ... Non-related extended family members ... A licensed foster home
steps: Same parents guide, placement list.

title: Removal
statement: When a child is taken out of the home to keep them safe.
source_says: Take your child from you if they think the child is in immediate danger.
steps: Same parents guide.

title: Resource Family
statement: The name California now uses for an approved foster home.
source_says: A licensed foster home (now known as resource family home) or shelter
steps: Opened parents guide and WIC 16519.5 on public.law.

title: Resource Family
statement: A resource family can be a relative, a family friend, or a foster parent who is not related.
source_says: a county shall approve resource families in lieu of approving relative and nonrelative extended family members
steps: Opened WIC 16519.5 on public.law; one process replaces foster home licensing and relative and NREFM approval.

title: Resource Family
statement: They are approved through one process called Resource Family Approval, which includes a home check and background checks.
source_says: unified, family friendly, and child-centered resource family approval process ... A home and grounds evaluation to ensure the health and safety of children
steps: Same page. Criminal record clearance by fingerprints also required.

title: Resource Family
statement: A family that is approved to care for a child in foster care. It can be relatives or foster parents.
source_says: A resource family shall be considered eligible to provide foster care for children in out-of-home placement
steps: Same page.

title: Resource Family Approval (RFA)
statement: The single approval process California uses for anyone who wants to care for a child in foster care, including relatives.
source_says: unified, family friendly, and child-centered resource family approval process
steps: Opened WIC 16519.5 on public.law (verified Nov. 2026). Heads up: also opened WIC 16519.3, which tells CDSS to adopt a simplified approval process for relative caregivers 'no later than January 1, 2027', if federal funding allows. Recheck this entry in early 2027.

title: Resource Family Approval (RFA)
statement: It includes a home check, background checks, and training.
source_says: Ensuring that a resource family applicant completes a minimum of 12 hours of preapproval caregiver training
steps: Same page; home and grounds evaluation and fingerprint background check also listed.

title: Resource Family Approval (RFA)
statement: The steps to get approved to care for a child in foster care.
source_says: unified, family friendly, and child-centered resource family approval process
steps: Same page.

title: RFA
statement: Resource Family Approval. The process for getting approved to care for a child in foster care.
source_says: unified, family friendly, and child-centered resource family approval process
steps: Opened WIC 16519.5 on public.law.

title: RFA
statement: The steps to get approved to care for a foster child.
source_says: unified, family friendly, and child-centered resource family approval process
steps: Same page.

title: Placement
statement: Where a child lives when not with their parents - could be foster home, relative, or group home.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet p. 9; Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: placed in a foster (resource) home, group home, or with relatives
steps: Entry has no source. Opened booklet p. 9 ('Decide where your child should live (this is called placement)') and the children and youth guide on selfhelp.courts.ca.gov.

title: Placement
statement: Where a child lives when they are not with their parents.
source_says: Decide where your child should live (this is called placement).
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 9.

title: Reunification
statement: The goal of returning children to their parents after the issues that led to removal have been addressed.
source_says: Reunification means getting your child returned and your family back together.
steps: Entry has no source. Opened booklet PDF p. 11 (PDF text shows the word with a dropped ligature). Also 42 USC 671(a)(15)(B): 'to make it possible for a child to safely return to the child's home'.

title: Reunification
statement: When a child goes back home to their parents.
source_says: Reunification means getting your child returned and your family back together.
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Reunification Services
statement: Services provided by the county to help parents resolve the problems that led to their child's removal.
source_says: the juvenile court shall order the social worker to provide child welfare services to the child
steps: Opened WIC 361.5 on public.law, subdivision (a). Subdivision (b) lists cases where services 'need not be provided'.

title: Reunification Services
statement: These might include parenting classes, counseling, substance abuse treatment, anger management, etc.
source_says: a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 10.

title: Reunification Services
statement: Most parents get about one year if they keep making progress.
source_says: Most of the time, you will have a year to complete your requirements if you keep making progress.
steps: Opened parents guide; WIC 361.5(a)(1)(A) on public.law: services end '12 months after the date the child entered foster care'.

title: Reunification Services
statement: If the child is under 3, it may be only 6 months.
source_says: court-ordered services shall be provided for a period of 6 months from the dispositional hearing
steps: Same WIC 361.5 page, (a)(1)(B). Booklet p. 11 says the same.

title: Reunification Services
statement: Help the county gives parents so their child can come home, like classes and counseling.
source_says: a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes
steps: Same booklet page and WIC 361.5(a).

title: Review Hearing
statement: Regular court dates (every 6 months) where the judge checks on the family's progress.
source_says: shall be reviewed periodically as determined by the court but no less frequently than once every six months
steps: Entry has no source. Opened WIC 366 on public.law and the parents guide ('the court will have a hearing every 6 months').

title: Review Hearing
statement: A court date every 6 months where the judge checks how things are going.
source_says: the court will have a hearing every 6 months.
steps: Opened parents guide.

title: Right to Counsel
statement: Parents and children in dependency court have the right to a lawyer.
source_says: the court shall appoint counsel for the parent or guardian
steps: Opened WIC 317 on public.law, subdivisions (a) to (c).

title: Right to Counsel
statement: If your child is removed from your home, or the county is asking to remove your child, and you cannot pay for a lawyer, the judge must appoint one for you.
source_says: or the petitioning agency is recommending that the child be placed in out-of-home care ... the court shall appoint counsel for the parent or guardian
steps: Same page, (b). Only exception stated is a knowing and intelligent waiver.

title: Right to Counsel
statement: In other cases the judge may appoint one.
source_says: the court may appoint counsel as provided in this section.
steps: Same page, (a)(1).

title: Right to Counsel
statement: The judge must give the child a lawyer unless the judge finds the child would not benefit from one.
source_says: the court shall appoint counsel for the child or nonminor dependent ... would not benefit from the appointment of counsel
steps: Same page, (c)(1).

title: Right to Counsel
statement: The court may ask later whether a parent can pay back some of the cost.
source_says: shall be liable for the cost to the county or the court, whichever entity incurred the expenses
steps: Opened WIC 903.1 on public.law. Parent is liable for cost of appointed counsel; (b) no liability if the petition is dismissed at or before the jurisdictional hearing. Ability-to-pay steps are in other sections not opened.

title: Right to Counsel
statement: Parents and children each get a lawyer in almost every case, even if they cannot pay.
source_says: If you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge will assign one to you. Most counties will also assign a lawyer for your child.
steps: Opened parents guide and WIC 317. 'Almost every case' is not a phrase in either source, but it matches the must-appoint rules in 317(b) and (c).

title: Right to Visitation
statement: When the judge orders reunification services, the judge must also order visits between you and your child, as often as possible, unless visits would put your child in danger.
source_says: Visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child. ... No visitation order shall jeopardize the safety of the child.
steps: Searched WIC 362.1, opened public.law page.

title: Right to Visitation
statement: Visits may be supervised at first.
source_says: Want to ask the court to change your supervised visits to unsupervised visits
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 33. It shows visits can be supervised and later changed. WIC 362.1 itself does not mention supervision.

title: Right to Visitation
statement: If the judge does not order services, the judge can still allow visits.
source_says: may continue to permit the parent to visit the child unless it finds that visitation would be detrimental
steps: Opened WIC 361.5 on public.law, subdivision (f).

title: Right to Visitation
statement: The court sets the visit schedule.
source_says: the judge will make orders about when and where you can visit your child.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 9.

title: Right to Visitation
statement: If you get services, you get visits with your child unless visits are not safe.
source_says: No visitation order shall jeopardize the safety of the child.
steps: Same WIC 362.1 page.

title: Safety Plan
statement: An agreement made with the agency about steps to keep a child safe without removing them from home.
source_name: CDSS All County Information Notice I-62-16
source_says: emphasizing that a plan is required in order for the child to remain in the home
steps: Entry source is only 'CDSS Policy'. Searched cdss.ca.gov, opened ACIN I-62-16. Plan form needs 'Signature lines for family members, the worker and his/her supervisor'.

title: Safety Plan
statement: May include having a relative stay with the family, attending services, or other protective measures.
source_says: Use of family, neighbors, or other individuals in the community as safety resources
steps: Same notice, list of safety interventions.

title: Safety Plan
statement: An agreement on steps to keep a child safe at home, so they do not have to be removed.
source_says: emphasizing that a plan is required in order for the child to remain in the home
steps: Same notice.

title: School of Origin
statement: The school a child was going to when they were removed or moved.
source_says: the school that the foster child attended when permanently housed or the school in which the foster child was last enrolled
steps: Opened Education Code 48853.5 on public.law. A school attended in the last 15 months that the child is connected to can also count.

title: School of Origin
statement: Children in foster care have the right to stay in their school of origin, even if their new home is in another area, when that is best for them.
source_says: shall allow the foster child to continue the foster child's education in the school of origin ... for the duration of the jurisdiction of the court.
steps: Same page. Right can be waived only in the child's best interests with agreement of the child and the education decision maker.

title: School of Origin
statement: The school you were already going to. You have the right to stay there.
source_name: CDE Foster Youth Education Rights; Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: You have the right to stay in the same school after you move to a new foster care placement.
steps: Searched cde.ca.gov, opened Foster Youth Education Rights. Children and youth guide: 'you have the right to stay at your school'.

title: Service Provider
statement: A person or program that gives the services in your case plan, like parenting classes, counseling, drug treatment, or anger management.
source_says: a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 10.

title: Service Provider
statement: Providers may report your attendance and progress to the social worker.
steps: Asked the booklet PDF twice for any text on providers reporting attendance or progress; it has none. Also not in the parents guide or the Judicial Council hearing outline. The web search budget for this run ran out before another source could be looked for.
fix: Keep only if a source is found. Safer wording: Your social worker may ask your providers how you are doing and tell the judge.

title: Service Provider
statement: If a program is not working for you, talk to the staff and your social worker instead of quitting.
source_says: If your social worker referred you to a program and it isn't working, don't just quit!
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 24.

title: Service Provider
statement: The people who run your classes, counseling, or treatment.
source_says: a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Services
statement: Programs parents may be required to complete, like parenting classes, counseling, or drug treatment.
source_says: the court may order you to do certain things before you can get your child back.
steps: Entry has no source. Opened booklet PDF p. 10 and p. 32 (reunification requirements).

title: Services
statement: Programs parents may have to finish, like parenting classes or counseling.
source_says: a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes
steps: Same booklet.

title: Settlement Conference
statement: A meeting before a trial where the lawyers and parties try to agree on some or all of the issues so a trial is not needed.
source_says: may meet privately with the judge to try to come to an agreement about what is best for your child.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 32. Note the booklet says it is 'the lawyers and the social worker' who meet with the judge; it does not say parents sit in.

title: Settlement Conference
statement: The judge can order one.
source_says: The judge may tell everyone to come back to court for a settlement conference.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 6.

title: Settlement Conference
statement: A meeting to try to agree before a trial.
source_says: This is a meeting that takes place before the court makes orders for your child
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Sibling
statement: A brother or sister, including half-brothers and half-sisters.
source_says: by blood, adoption, or affinity ... through a common legal or biological parent
steps: Opened WIC 16002 on public.law, subdivision (g).

title: Sibling
statement: Children who are removed have the right to visit their siblings, and the county should try to place siblings together.
source_says: Children removed from their homes have the right to visit their siblings, half-siblings, and adult siblings.
steps: Opened relatives guide. WIC 16002(b): agency 'shall make a diligent effort' to place siblings together. WIC 362.1(a)(2): sibling visits unless the court finds they are not safe.

title: Sibling
statement: A sibling can use form JV-180 to ask the judge for visits, and an adult sibling can ask for the child to live with them.
source_says: An adult sibling can also use this form to ask the court to have their sibling placed in their care.
steps: Opened relatives guide: 'Request to Change Court Order' (form JV-180) to 'ask the court to recognize the sibling relationship and give the sibling visitation'.

title: Sibling
statement: A brother or sister. Brothers and sisters have the right to see each other.
source_says: Children removed from their homes have the right to visit their siblings, half-siblings, and adult siblings.
steps: Same relatives guide.

title: Six-Month Review Hearing
statement: The first review hearing, held about six months after the disposition hearing.
source_says: At the review hearing held 6 months after the initial dispositional hearing
steps: Opened WIC 366.21 on public.law. Must also be no later than 12 months after the child entered foster care.

title: Six-Month Review Hearing
statement: The judge checks whether the county gave you the services in your case plan and whether you are working on it.
source_says: have been provided or offered to the parent or legal guardian
steps: Same page: (e)(8) court decides whether reasonable services were provided or offered; (e)(3) looks at whether the parent took part regularly and made progress.

title: Six-Month Review Hearing
statement: The judge can return your child, order more services, or end services.
source_says: Decide whether to return your child to you, dismiss the case, or continue with the plan as ordered.
steps: Opened booklet p. 12 and WIC 366.21(e): return unless substantial risk of detriment; services initiated, continued, or terminated.

title: Six-Month Review Hearing
statement: If your child was under 3 when removed, this hearing matters most, because services may be limited to six months.
source_says: If the child was under three years of age on the date of the initial removal
steps: Same page, (e)(3): court may set a 366.26 hearing within 120 days if the parent did not take part and make progress.

title: Six-Month Review Hearing
statement: The check-in hearing about six months in. The judge looks at how things are going.
source_says: At the review hearing held 6 months after the initial dispositional hearing
steps: Same page.

title: Social Worker
statement: A county worker assigned to your family's case.
source_says: The social worker assigned to your case will come up with the reunification services, with your input.
steps: Opened parents guide. Also opened WIC 16501 on public.law: 'The county shall provide child welfare services'. WIC 16501 does not use the words social worker.

title: Social Worker
statement: Social workers look into reports about a child's safety, decide whether to ask the court to step in
source_says: They are required to investigate these reports.
steps: Opened parents guide. After investigating, the worker may take no action, offer free services, file a petition, or remove the child.

title: Social Worker
statement: write the reports the judge reads before each hearing, and recommend what the judge should order.
source_says: The court report is prepared by CPS describing what is happening with you and your family ... what the social worker is recommending the court to order
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 29.

title: Social Worker
statement: They also set up your case plan and services, arrange visits
source_says: you can also ask the social worker to set up frequent visits with your child
steps: Opened parents guide; same page says the social worker comes up with the reunification services.

title: Social Worker
statement: look for relatives who could care for your child
source_says: The social worker is required to ask you about any relatives who might be able to take care of your child.
steps: Opened booklet p. 10 and WIC 309 on public.law (30-day search for relatives).

title: Social Worker
statement: and visit your child every month.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for children and youth; CDSS ACL 13-13
source_says: They also have to visit you every month to make sure everything is going well.
steps: Opened children and youth guide. CDSS ACL 13-13 also says children in foster care are to be 'visited by their caseworkers each and every month'.

title: Social Worker
statement: The social worker works for the county, not for you, but staying in touch with them matters.
source_says: This is the agency that has the social workers who help on your case ... Work with your social worker and keep in touch with him or her, too.
steps: Opened booklet p. 13 footnote and p. 22. No source says 'not for you' in those words; the worker belongs to the county agency.

title: Social Worker
statement: If you cannot reach yours, call the county agency's main number and ask for a supervisor.
source_says: If your social worker isn't returning your calls, locate the main number for your
steps: Opened parents guide; sentence goes on to say ask for a supervisor.

title: Social Worker
statement: The county worker who checks on a child's safety, sets up help, and reports to the judge.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for parents; booklet p. 29
source_says: They are required to investigate these reports.
steps: Same sources as the definition.

title: Social Worker Supervisor
statement: The boss of your social worker at the county agency. If you cannot reach your social worker, or you have a problem you cannot work out with them, call the agency's main number and ask for the supervisor.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for children and youth; Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: locate the main number for your [county's social services agency] and ask for a supervisor.
steps: Opened both guides. Both give this step for a worker who does not call back; neither covers 'a problem you cannot work out'.

title: Social Worker Supervisor
statement: Tell your lawyer too.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: locate the main number for your [county's social services agency] and ask for a supervisor.
steps: Same children and youth guide; next to this line it suggests telling your lawyer and the judge in court (seen as a summary, not a direct quote).

title: Social Worker Supervisor
statement: Your social worker's boss. Ask for them if you cannot reach your social worker.
source_says: If your social worker isn't returning your calls, locate the main number for your
steps: Opened parents guide.

title: Status Review
statement: Another name for a review hearing. You may also hear dependency status review, DSR, or periodic review.
source_says: which in different courts can also be called status review hearings, periodic review hearings, or DSR hearings.
steps: Opened parents guide.

title: Status Review
statement: They are held every six months while the case is open.
source_says: During the time your child is in the system, the court will have a hearing every 6 months.
steps: Same parents guide.

title: Status Review
statement: Another name for the six-month check-in hearings.
source_says: These court hearings are dependency status review (DSR) hearings,
steps: Same parents guide.

title: STRTP
statement: Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program.
source_says: "Short-term residential therapeutic program" means a residential facility operated by a public agency
steps: Searched HSC 1502, opened public.law page; paragraph (a)(18) as cited. WIC 11400(ad) also defines it.

title: STRTP
statement: A licensed group setting that gives intensive treatment and round-the-clock supervision for a short time to children who cannot safely live in a family home right now.
source_says: provides short-term, specialized, and intensive therapeutic and 24-hour care and supervision to children.
steps: Opened cdss.ca.gov facility information page. CDSS Continuum of Care Reform page: for 'children and youth requiring highly intensive 24-hour supervision and treatment'.

title: STRTP
statement: STRTPs replaced most group homes in California.
source_name: CDSS ACL 16-79; CDSS Continuum of Care Reform page
source_says: eventually replace the Group Home (GH) rate classification level (RCL) structure
steps: Opened ACL 16-79 (group homes may apply to be licensed as STRTPs; no new group home rates) and the CCR page ('Group care will be primarily utilized only for short-term residential treatment centers'). Neither gives a count; group home is still a license type.

title: STRTP
statement: A place with staff where a child stays for a short time to get extra help.
source_says: provides short-term, specialized, and intensive therapeutic and 24-hour care and supervision to children.
steps: Same CDSS page.

title: Supervised Visit
statement: A visit where another adult stays with you and your child the whole time.
source_says: If you have been supervising visits between the child and a parent
steps: Opened the Judicial Council caregiver primer; it describes a third person supervising parent visits. No opened source defines the term or says 'the whole time'. The booklet uses 'supervised visits' without defining it.

title: Supervised Visit
statement: Visits often start out supervised.
steps: Opened both cited sources. WIC 362.1 does not address supervision and the booklet does not say how often visits start supervised. The web search budget for this run ran out before another source could be looked for.
fix: Visits may be supervised at first.

title: Supervised Visit
statement: As things go well, you can ask to move to visits without a monitor, and your lawyer can ask the judge to change the order.
source_says: Want to ask the court to change your supervised visits to unsupervised visits
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 33 (request to change a court order).

title: Supervised Visit
statement: A visit where another adult stays in the room.
source_says: If you have been supervising visits between the child and a parent
steps: Same primer.

title: Termination of Parental Rights
statement: A permanent legal action that ends the parent-child relationship.
source_says: you are no longer legally your child's parent and have no legal rights or responsibilities to him or her.
steps: Opened booklet p. 16 and WIC 366.26 on public.law: order 'shall be conclusive and binding' and the court has 'no power to set aside, change, or modify it'.

title: Termination of Parental Rights
statement: It is decided at the 366.26 hearing.
source_says: Terminate the rights of the parent or parents and order that the child be placed for adoption
steps: Opened WIC 366.26 on public.law.

title: Termination of Parental Rights
statement: The judge can end your rights even if you are not there, so go to that hearing and talk with your lawyer before it.
source_name: Form JV-300, Notice of Hearing on Selection of a Permanent Plan
source_says: The court will proceed with this hearing whether or not you are present.
steps: WIC 366.26 and WIC 294 on public.law do not say this. Opened Judicial Council form JV-300 on courts.ca.gov, which does.

title: Termination of Parental Rights
statement: After parental rights are terminated, the child can be adopted and the parent no longer has legal rights or responsibilities for the child.
source_says: you are no longer legally your child's parent and have no legal rights or responsibilities to him or her.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 16.

title: Termination of Parental Rights
statement: When a judge ends a parent's legal rights to their child for good. After that, the child can be adopted.
source_says: Terminate the rights of the parent or parents and order that the child be placed for adoption
steps: Same WIC 366.26 page.

title: Termination of Services
statement: When the judge ends the reunification services the county was providing.
source_says: does not have to provide any more services for you. This is what's called termination of services.
steps: Opened booklet PDF p. 13.

title: Termination of Services
statement: This is not the same as ending your parental rights.
source_says: Termination of services is NOT the same as termination of parental rights.
steps: Same page.

title: THP
statement: Transitional Housing Program
source_name: CDSS, Transitional Housing Programs for Foster Youth in California
source_says: The Transitional Housing Program (THP) provides current and former foster youth additional supports they need
steps: Searched CDSS transitional housing programs, opened the CDSS page, read the opening paragraph.

title: THP
statement: housing assistance for youth aging out of foster care or young adults who were in foster care.
source_name: CDSS, Transitional Housing Programs for Foster Youth in California
source_says: Provides housing options for young adults who exited foster care ... on or after their 18th birthday.
steps: Same CDSS page. It lists THP-NMD for ages 18-21 in Extended Foster Care and THP-Plus for young adults who left care at 18 or later.

title: THP
statement: Helps with the transition to independent living.
source_name: CDSS, Transitional Housing Programs for Foster Youth in California
source_says: to successfully transition to independence while reducing the risks of homelessness,
steps: Same CDSS page, opening paragraph.

title: THP
statement: Housing help for young people leaving foster care.
source_name: CDSS, Transitional Housing Programs for Foster Youth in California
source_says: By providing housing, life skills training, and guidance, the program helps Nonminor Dependents build a strong foundation
steps: Same CDSS page, opening paragraph.

title: THP
statement: Source cited: WIC §16522
source_says: The State Department of Social Services shall license transitional housing placement providers
steps: Searched WIC 16522, opened the public.law page. The section is a licensing rule for providers (foster children at least 16, and THP-Plus providers). It names the programs but does not describe who gets housing help or that it is for young adults who left care. The entry itself is supported by the CDSS page.
fix: Keep the entry. Change the source to the CDSS Transitional Housing Programs page, with WIC 16522 as the licensing rule only.

title: TILP
statement: Transitional Independent Living Plan.
source_says: the case plan shall include the transitional independent living plan (TILP),
steps: Searched WIC 16501.1 transitional independent living plan, opened the public.law page, read paragraph (16)(A)(ii).

title: TILP
statement: A written plan a youth in foster care makes with their social worker
source_says: The case plan shall be developed with the child or nonminor dependent
steps: Same public.law page, clause (ii). Also opened CDSS form TILP 1 (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/cdssweb/entres/forms/english/tilp1.pdf), which has signature lines for the youth, caregiver and social worker or probation officer.

title: TILP
statement: starting at 16
source_says: When appropriate, for a child who is 16 years of age or older and, commencing January 1, 2012, for a nonminor dependent,
steps: Same page. Clause (i) covers ages 14 and 15 with a written description of services; the TILP itself is required at 16 and older.

title: TILP
statement: that lists their goals for adulthood and the services that will help, like school, work, housing, and money skills.
source_says: a written description of the programs and services that will help the child, consistent with the child’s best interests, to prepare for the transition from foster care to successful adulthood,
steps: Same page. Examples checked on CDSS form TILP 1 (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/cdssweb/entres/forms/english/tilp1.pdf), which lists ILP Education, ILP Career/Job Guidance, ILP Money Management and ILP Transitional Housing.

title: TILP
statement: Your plan for getting ready for adult life, starting at 16.
source_says: When appropriate, for a child who is 16 years of age or older ... the case plan shall include the transitional independent living plan (TILP),
steps: Same public.law page, same clause.

title: Transcript
statement: The word-for-word written record of what was said at a hearing, typed by the court reporter.
source_says: the official court reporter or other authorized transcriber must prepare a transcript of the proceedings ... and must certify that the proceedings have been correctly reported and transcribed.
steps: Searched rule 5.532 court reporter transcripts, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read subdivision (c).

title: Transcript
statement: It is used when a case is appealed.
source_says: the oral proceedings at any hearing that resulted in the order or judgment being appealed.
steps: Searched rule 8.407 record on appeal juvenile reporter's transcript, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page (Record on appeal), read subdivision (b) on what the reporter's transcript must contain.

title: Transcript
statement: The typed record of everything said in court.
source_says: an official court reporter or other authorized reporting procedure must record all proceedings.
steps: Same rule 5.532 page, subdivisions (a) and (c).

title: Tribal Customary Adoption
statement: A kind of adoption for a Native American child that is done through the customs and laws of the child's tribe.
source_says: “tribal customary adoption” means adoption by and through the tribal custom, traditions, or law of an Indian child’s tribe.
steps: Searched WIC 366.24 tribal customary adoption, opened the public.law page, read (a)(1).

title: Tribal Customary Adoption
statement: Unlike other adoptions, it does not require ending the birth parents' rights.
source_says: Termination of parental rights is not required to effect the tribal customary adoption.
steps: Same public.law page. Booklet p. 17 also says it is as permanent as adoption without requiring termination of your parental rights.

title: Tribal Customary Adoption
statement: An adoption done the tribe's way. Parents' rights do not have to end.
source_says: Termination of parental rights is not required to effect the tribal customary adoption.
steps: Same public.law page, (a)(1).

title: Tribe
statement: If your child is or may be a Native American child, the child's tribe has rights in the case under the Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA).
source_says: The child's tribe has the same rights as you and your child
steps: Searched for the booklet on courts.ca.gov, opened the PDF, read the ICWA section on p. 30.

title: Tribe
statement: The social worker must notify the tribe.
source_says: The social worker must tell the child's tribe about your case.
steps: Booklet p. 30. Also opened WIC 224.3 on public.law (https://california.public.law/codes/ca_welf_and_inst_code_section_224.3): notice shall be sent to the parents, Indian custodian and the child's tribe.

title: Tribe
statement: The tribe can join the case at any time
source_says: have the right to intervene at any point in an Indian child custody proceeding.
steps: Searched WIC 224.4 tribe right to intervene, opened the public.law page, read the whole section.

title: Tribe
statement: send a representative to court
source_says: In a proceeding described by rule 5.480, a representative of the Indian child's tribe;
steps: Searched rule 5.530 persons present, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read the list in (b). The citation to (b)(7) is right.

title: Tribe
statement: and give its view on placement and the long-term plan.
source_name: Judicial Council ICWA Information Sheet: Tribal participation in State court; booklet p. 17
source_says: The tribe must be consulted with respect to the placement of the child.
steps: Opened the Judicial Council tribal participation fact sheet returned by search. It also says a tribal representative may submit written reports and recommendations to the court. Booklet p. 17 says the court asks the tribe whether tribal customary adoption is an appropriate permanent plan.

title: Tribe
statement: It can also offer services and support.
source_name: Judicial Council ICWA Information Sheet: Tribal participation in State court
source_says: must use the available resources of the tribe
steps: Same fact sheet, on case plans. It speaks of using the tribe's resources in the case plan, not in the words "offer services".

title: Tribe
statement: Only the tribe decides whether a child is a member or can be one.
source_says: A determination by an Indian tribe that a child is or is not a member or citizen of, ... that tribe ... shall be conclusive.
steps: Searched WIC 224.2 tribe membership conclusive, opened the public.law page, read (h). Booklet p. 30 says only tribes can decide if your child is an Indian child.

title: Tribe
statement: A Native American child's tribe gets told about the case and can take part in it.
source_says: The social worker must tell the child's tribe about your case.
steps: Booklet p. 30, which also says the tribe can choose to get involved in the case at any time.

title: Twelve-Month Review Hearing
statement: The review hearing held about a year after your child entered foster care.
source_says: The permanency hearing shall be held no later than 12 months after the date the child entered foster care
steps: Searched WIC 366.21 permanency hearing 12 months, opened the public.law page, read (f)(1).

title: Twelve-Month Review Hearing
statement: The judge decides whether your child can come home.
source_says: the court shall order the return of the child to the physical custody of their parent or legal guardian unless
steps: Same page, subdivision (f). The child goes home unless the court finds a substantial risk of detriment.

title: Twelve-Month Review Hearing
statement: If not, the judge decides whether to give you more time
source_says: Continue the case for up to 6 months for a permanency review hearing.
steps: Same page, (g)(1). More time needs specific findings and must fit within 18 months of removal.

title: Twelve-Month Review Hearing
statement: or to end services and set a hearing to choose a permanent plan.
source_says: Order that a hearing be held within 120 days, pursuant to Section 366.26, ... it shall also order the termination of reunification services to the parent or legal guardian.
steps: Same page, (g)(4) and (h). Note: (g)(5) is a third choice the entry does not list, an order that the child remain in foster care without a 366.26 hearing.

title: Twelve-Month Review Hearing
statement: The hearing about a year in. The judge decides if your child can come home.
source_says: The permanency hearing shall be held no later than 12 months after the date the child entered foster care
steps: Same page, (f)(1) and the return rule in (f).

title: Visit Monitor
statement: The person who stays with you and your child during a supervised visit.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy 0400-504.00, Family Time
source_says: Supervised family time is any contact between a child who is under the supervision of DCFS and a family member
steps: Searched who supervises dependency visits, opened the LA County DCFS policy returned by search. The policy says a DCFS-approved or court-ordered monitor must be present. This is one county's policy; no statewide source defines the term.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: It may be a social worker ... or a relative the county approves.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy 0400-504.00, Family Time
source_says: Family friend or relative agreed to by all parties, with whom the child is comfortable
steps: Same LA County policy. It also lists a CSW or other staff whose job includes family time supervision, and says DCFS must ensure the monitor meets minimum qualifications. One county only.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: a staff member at a visiting center
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy 0400-504.00; CDSS Visitation page
steps: The LA County policy lists staff, relatives or family friends, resource parents, FFA social workers and professional or therapeutic monitors, but I did not see visiting center staff named. The CDSS caregiver visitation page (https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/caregiver-advocacy-network/visitation) only mentions caregivers supervising. Court pages found were for family court, not dependency.
fix: It may be a social worker, another county worker, a paid monitor, your child's caregiver, or a relative or friend the county approves.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: The monitor may write notes about the visit that the social worker and judge can see.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy 0400-504.00, Family Time
source_says: All family time needs to be documented in the Contact Notebook, including any report back from a Monitor.
steps: Same LA County policy. It also says a report about the supervised family time should be produced if the court orders or asks for one. One county only.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: The adult who stays in the room during a supervised visit.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy 0400-504.00, Family Time
source_says: Supervised family time is any contact between a child who is under the supervision of DCFS and a family member
steps: Same LA County policy; a monitor must be present for supervised family time.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: Source cited: WIC §362.1; county practice varies
source_says: Visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child.
steps: Searched WIC 362.1, opened the public.law page and asked for any use of supervised, monitor or monitored. None of those words appear in the section. It is the general visiting law only.
fix: Source: county visiting policy and the judge's visiting order. WIC 362.1 is the general law on visits and does not talk about monitors.

title: Visitation
statement: Scheduled time for parents to spend with their children during the case.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; WIC 362.1(a)(1)(A)
source_says: the judge will make orders about when and where you can visit your child.
steps: Opened the self-help guide for parents (reached by redirect from a courts.ca.gov search result). Also opened WIC 362.1 on public.law: visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child. The entry has no source listed.

title: Visitation
statement: Set times when parents and children get to be together.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: the judge will make orders about when and where you can visit your child.
steps: Same self-help page.

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: A form parents can sign, often at the hospital when a baby is born
source_says: shall provide to the woman giving birth and shall attempt to provide, at the place of birth,
steps: Searched Family Code 7571 and 7573, opened the public.law page for 7571, read (a). It can also be signed later at child support offices, registrars, courts and welfare departments under (f).

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: that makes a person the child's legal parent.
source_says: that has been filed with the Department of Child Support Services is equivalent to a judgment of parentage of the child
steps: Opened Family Code 7573 on public.law. Under (c) the form takes effect on filing with the Department of Child Support Services, and (d) lists exceptions. Signing alone is not enough.
fix: A form parents can sign, often at the hospital when a baby is born. Once it is filed with the state, it makes a person the child's legal parent.

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: A person who signed one is usually treated as a presumed parent.
source_says: your spouse or the other parent who signed the form is probably your child's legal parent ... also called a presumed parent.
steps: Opened the booklet, p. 31. The booklet uses the older name, voluntary declaration of paternity.

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: A form parents sign that makes someone the legal parent.
source_says: a voluntary declaration of parentage takes effect on the filing of the document with the Department of Child Support Services.
steps: Same Family Code 7573 page. The form works once it is filed with the state, not just when signed.
fix: A form parents sign that makes someone the legal parent once it is filed with the state.

title: Voluntary Services
statement: Free services a social worker may offer a family without opening a court case.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; WIC 301(a)
source_says: Offer free services designed to help you learn how to parent your child more safely.
steps: Opened the self-help guide for parents; this is one of the choices listed after an investigation. Also opened WIC 301 on public.law: the social worker may act in lieu of filing a petition.

title: Voluntary Services
statement: The family agrees to take part
source_says: with consent of the child's parent or guardian
steps: Searched WIC 301 program of supervision, opened the public.law page, read (a).

title: Voluntary Services
statement: and the child usually stays home.
steps: WIC 301(a) points to services under WIC 16506 and 16507.3. Opened both on public.law. 16506 is about keeping the child in his or her own home. 16507.3 covers children placed voluntarily, limited to 180 days. No source opened says how often the child stays home, so "usually" could not be checked.
fix: The child can stay home while the family gets help. A parent can also agree to a short placement outside the home.

title: Voluntary Services
statement: If things do not improve, the county can still file a petition.
source_says: Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent the social worker from filing a petition pursuant to Section 332 when otherwise authorized by law.
steps: Same WIC 301 page. It also says that if the family has refused to cooperate with the services, the social worker may file a petition.

title: Voluntary Services
statement: Help a family agrees to take without going to court.
source_says: undertake a program of supervision of the child
steps: Same WIC 301 page: in lieu of filing a petition, with consent of the parent or guardian.

title: WIC
statement: Welfare and Institutions Code - California law that governs child welfare cases.
source_says: A child who comes within any of the following descriptions is within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court
steps: Searched and opened the public.law page titled California Welfare and Institutions Code section 300, the code section that starts dependency cases. The entry has no source listed.

title: WIC
statement: The California law book for child welfare cases.
source_says: A child who comes within any of the following descriptions is within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court
steps: Same public.law page, titled California Welfare and Institutions Code section 300.

title: WIC 300
statement: Welfare and Institutions Code Section 300 - the California law that defines the types of abuse and neglect that can bring a child under court protection.
source_says: A child who comes within any of the following descriptions is within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 300, read the opening sentence and subdivisions (a) through (j).

title: WIC 300
statement: Includes physical abuse, neglect, sexual abuse, and situations where a child is at risk of harm.
source_says: The child has been sexually abused, or there is a substantial risk that the child will be sexually abused
steps: Same page. (a) covers serious physical harm inflicted nonaccidentally, (b) failure or inability to adequately supervise or protect, (d) sexual abuse, and several subdivisions cover substantial risk.

title: WIC 300
statement: The law that lists the kinds of harm that let the court step in to protect a child.
source_says: A child who comes within any of the following descriptions is within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court
steps: Same public.law page.

title: Witness
statement: A person who answers questions under oath at a hearing.
source_says: Every witness before testifying shall take an oath or make an affirmation or declaration in the form provided by law,
steps: Searched Evidence Code 710, opened the public.law page. A child under 10 may be asked only to promise to tell the truth.

title: Witness
statement: If you disagree with what the county says and ask for a trial
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.684(a); Judicial Council booklet p. 7
source_says: the court must hold a contested hearing and determine whether the allegations in the petition are true.
steps: Searched rule 5.684 contested hearing, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read (a): this happens if the parent denies the petition. Booklet p. 7 says the judge will have a trial to review evidence and listen to witnesses.

title: Witness
statement: your lawyer ... can ... call witnesses.
source_says: The right to use the process of the court to bring in witnesses;
steps: Searched rule 5.534, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read (g)(1). (D) adds the right to present evidence to the court.

title: Witness
statement: county counsel can ... call witnesses.
steps: Rule 5.530(d) says county counsel or the district attorney must appear and represent the petitioner in section 300 cases. Rule 5.534(g)(1)(B) mentions the witnesses called to testify at the hearing. Rule 5.684 does not say who presents witnesses, and the booklet does not say who may call them. No page opened says in words that county counsel may call witnesses. WIC 318.5 could not be opened on an approved site.
fix: Each side can bring witnesses. Your lawyer can ask the county's witnesses questions too.

title: Witness
statement: A witness could be the social worker, a counselor, a relative, or you.
source_says: every person, irrespective of age, is qualified to be a witness
steps: Searched Evidence Code 700, opened the public.law page. Rule 5.534(g)(1)(B) also gives the right to cross-examine the persons who prepared reports submitted by the petitioner.

title: Witness
statement: Someone who answers questions in court after promising to tell the truth.
source_says: Every witness before testifying shall take an oath or make an affirmation or declaration in the form provided by law,
steps: Same Evidence Code 710 page.

title: Witness
statement: Source cited: Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You
source_says: the judge will have a trial to review evidence and listen to witnesses before deciding what needs to be done.
steps: Opened the booklet and asked for every passage on witnesses, testifying and trials. It mentions witnesses at a trial but does not define witness, mention an oath, say who may call witnesses, or list who can be one. It never mentions county counsel.
fix: Keep the booklet for the trial part. Add Evidence Code 700 and 710 and Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(g) as sources.

title: Writ Petition
statement: A fast way to challenge the judge's order setting a .26 hearing.
source_says: Rules 8.450-8.452 and 8.490 govern writ petitions to review orders setting a hearing under Welfare and Institutions Code section 366.26.
steps: Searched rule 8.450 notice of intent, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page. (b) says the rules aim to get writ petitions decided within the 120-day period for holding the 366.26 hearing.

title: Writ Petition
statement: You usually have only 7 days from that order to file a notice that you plan to do this.
source_says: the notice of intent must be filed within 7 days after the date of the order setting the hearing.
steps: Same rule page, (e)(4). 7 days applies if the party was present at the hearing. It is 12 days from mailing if told only by mail, 17 or 27 days if mailed out of state or out of the country, and 10 more days if a referee made the order.

title: Writ Petition
statement: It's more urgent than a regular appeal.
source_says: must be filed within 60 days after the rendition of the judgment or the making of the order being appealed.
steps: Searched rule 8.406 time to appeal, opened the courts.ca.gov rule page. A regular appeal has 60 days; the writ notice has 7.

title: Writ Petition
statement: Your attorney should tell you if you need to file a writ.
source_name: WIC 366.26(l)(3)(A); Cal. Rules of Court, rules 5.590(b), 8.450(e)(3)
source_says: the court must advise all parties and, if present, the child's parent, guardian, or adult relative.
steps: Opened rule 5.590(b), rule 8.450 and WIC 366.26(l) (https://california.public.law/codes/welfare_and_institutions_code_section_366.26). The sources put the duty to tell you on the court: out loud to those present, by mail from the clerk to others. The notice must be signed by the party or the attorney of record. WIC 366.26(l)(2) says not filing on time ends the right to appeal that order. No source opened says the attorney must tell you.
fix: The judge must tell you about the writ when the .26 hearing is set. If you were not in court, the clerk mails you a notice. Do not wait to be told. Tell your lawyer right away that you want to file. If you miss the deadline, you lose the right to appeal that order.

title: Writ Petition
statement: A fast way to ask a higher court to look at the judge's order setting a .26 hearing. You usually have only 7 days to start, so tell your lawyer right away.
source_says: the notice of intent must be filed within 7 days after the date of the order setting the hearing.
steps: Same rule 8.450 page. (b) refers to the reviewing courts deciding writ petitions on their merits. The citation to CRC 8.450 and WIC 366.26(l) supports the entry.
